# Glossary 

- **TP_calls**: eris’s nearest gene on a side that is the right gene --> because the truth only reported one flanks gene, that is why we **ignore the others when calculating precision**.
- **FN_wrong_side**: eris found the gene but reported it on the other side, e.g. downstream instead of upstream. It counts as a miss.
- **FP_wrong_side**: The same wrong-side mistake seen from eris’s side: the gene is real but sits on the wrong side. It counts as a false call, so one wrong-side mistake costs both recall and precision.
- **FP_unplaceable**: eris reported a gene whose DNA can’t be found in the reference genome, usually a gene cut off at a contig end in a GFA assembly. It can’t match anything, so it counts as a false call.

Wrong side cause both FP and FN.

# Main findings

* eris finds about three quarters of IS–CDS relations on the complete genome; fragmented assemblies cost about 0.12–0.15 F1.
* Upstream is consistently more accurate than downstream. Almost all misses come from gene calling, not from the graph walk: allowing 20 hops instead of 3 recovers only 0–2 relations per assembly.
* Often the right gene is found but a wrong gene sits nearer the IS. On the complete genome this happens for 17 of the 85 relations found: either the IS's own transposase overhangs its end and is reported as a disrupted flank, or pyfgs calls a short ORF (69–234 bp) that RefSeq does not annotate. Counting only eris's nearest gene, recall drops to 0.58 / 0.38 / 0.35.
* Disrupted calls are poor, especially on GFAs, partly because of the same transposase overhang.


# IS–CDS relation validation

Scores from [eris-validation](https://github.com/Victoriasja18/eris-validation): for each IS, did eris report the right CDS **upstream** and **downstream**, at the right **distance**, with the right **effect** (disrupted)?

- Truth: `ec958_IS_cds_relations.tsv` (117 relations; 94 on the chromosome for the simulated GFA).
- eris: Dimas's main (`e4c6dbd`), collapse mode, `--hops 3`, `min_coverage 0.30`.

```bash
cd ../../eris-validation
uv run snakemake --cores 4
```

```{python}
import pandas as pd

RESULTS = "../result/eris_validation"
ASSEMBLIES = {"complete": "Complete genome (FASTA)", "simulated": "Simulated GFA", "real": "Real-reads GFA"}

metrics = pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/metrics.tsv", sep="\t")
details = pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/details.tsv", sep="\t")
for table in (metrics, details):
    table["assembly"] = table["assembly_type"].map(ASSEMBLIES)
```

## Precision, recall and F1

Side: recall is over the truth relations; precision is over eris's nearest flank on each side (per graph branch).
A flank on the wrong side counts as a miss on its true side and a false call on the side reported.
Distance: per band (overlapping, near 0–150 bp, far), over relations found on their side.
Effect: disrupted only; eris `TRUNCATED` counts as disrupted.

- Recall = TP / (TP + FN) over the truth relations. 
- Precision = TP_calls / (TP_calls + FP) over eris's calls; for side and effect these are eris's nearest flanks, so TP_calls can be lower than TP (when a wrong gene, such as the IS's own transposase or a short ORF, sits nearer the IS than the true CDS, the true CDS still counts as found for recall, but eris's call is an FP).

```{python}
(metrics.drop(columns=["genome", "assembly_type"])
        .set_index(["assembly", "dimension", "class"])
        .style.format("{:.2f}", subset=["precision", "recall", "f1"], na_rep="–"))
```

```{python}
other = {("side", "both", "pooled_recall"): "Pooled recall (either side)",
         ("side", "both", "wrong_side"): "Found only on the wrong side",
         ("side", "both", "miss_gene"): "Misses: wrong/absent gene",
         ("side", "both", "miss_budget"): "Misses: hops budget (found with --hops 20)",
         ("side", "both", "unplaceable"): "Flank genes not placeable on the reference",
         ("distance", "all", "agreement"): "Distance band agreement",
         ("distance", "all", "median_abs_error"): "Median distance error (bp)",
         ("distance", "all", "within_10bp"): "Distance within 10 bp"}
value = details.set_index(["dimension", "class", "metric", "assembly"])["value"]
summary = pd.DataFrame({name: [value[(*k, name)] for k in other] for name in ASSEMBLIES.values()},
                       index=list(other.values()))
counts = [name for name in summary.index if not name.startswith(("Pooled", "Distance", "Median"))]
summary.style.format("{:.2f}").format("{:.0f}", subset=pd.IndexSlice[counts, :])
```

## Confusion matrices

Rows are the truth, columns are eris. `no_truth` = a flank eris reported that is in no truth relation.

```{python}
from IPython.display import display, Markdown

for kind in ("side", "distance", "effect"):
    display(Markdown(f"### {kind.capitalize()}"))
    for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items():
        display(Markdown(f"**{name}**"))
        display(pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/EC958/{a}/{kind}_confusion.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0))
```

## Which CDS were predicted wrong

Every truth relation eris missed (`FN`, `FN_wrong_side`), every false first flank (`FP`, `FP_wrong_side`,
`FP_unplaceable`), and found relations whose distance band or effect is wrong.

Full tables: `progress/result/eris_validation/EC958/<assembly>/relations.tsv`; the quick summary is `progress/result/eris_validation/metrics.tsv`.

```{python}
relations = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/EC958/{a}/relations.tsv", sep="\t").assign(assembly=name)
                       for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items()], ignore_index=True)
wrong = relations[(relations["status"] != "TP") | (relations["distance_band_ok"] == False)
                  | (relations["effect_ok"] == False)]
pd.crosstab(wrong["status"], wrong["assembly"])[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())]
```

```{python}
columns = ["assembly", "status", "side", "is_id", "locus_tag", "gene", "product", "truth_distance", "truth_effect",
           "eris_target", "eris_gene", "eris_side", "eris_distance", "eris_effect", "distance_band_ok", "effect_ok",
           "miss_cause"]
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None, "display.max_colwidth", None)
wrong[columns].sort_values(["assembly", "status", "is_id"]).reset_index(drop=True).fillna("")
```
